method: Three cgroup v1 settings are turned into the v2 file that carries the same limit. cpu.shares (2 to 262144, default 1024) becomes cpu.weight (1 to 10000, default 100) with the formula adopted by runc 1.3.2 and crun 1.23: weight = ceil(10^(L^2/612 + 125L/612 - 7/34)), where L = log2(shares); it is exact at 2 -> 1, 1024 -> 100 and 262144 -> 10000, and every shares value from 2 to 262144 maps to a weight in range with all 10000 weights reachable. The older KEP-2254 linear mapping weight = 1 + floor((shares - 2) * 9999 / 262142) is shown beside it and gives 39 for 1024 shares, which is why it was replaced. cpu.cfs_quota_us (-1 for no limit, otherwise a whole number of microseconds) and cpu.cfs_period_us (1000 to 1000000, default 100000) collapse into one cpu.max line written as $MAX $PERIOD with the quota first, and -1 becomes the literal max; the CPU equivalent is quota divided by period, capped by neither the page nor a CPU count. memory.limit_in_bytes becomes memory.max with the same byte count, and -1 becomes max. Every field accepts whole numbers only: surrounding spaces, a leading minus sign and leading zeros are accepted, while decimal points, unit suffixes and exponents are refused with a message that names the field, its range and the unlimited sentinel. Values above 9007199254740991 bytes or 1000000000000 microseconds are refused instead of being rounded. The page states that a weight is a relative share among runnable siblings rather than a reservation, and everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Linux kernel cgroup v2 documentation: cpu.weight defaults to 100 in the range 1 to 10000, cpu.max is a two-value file in the format $MAX $PERIOD defaulting to max 100000, and memory.max defaults to max.
Linux kernel CFS bandwidth control documentation covers the cgroup v1 cpu.cfs_quota_us and cpu.cfs_period_us pair that cpu.max replaces.
systemd cgroup-util.h defines the ranges used here: cpu shares 2 to 262144 with a default of 1024, and CPU weight 1 to 10000 with a default of 100.
Kubernetes blog, New Conversion from cgroup v1 CPU Shares to v2 CPU Weight: records the KEP-2254 linear formula, the replacement logarithmic formula, and its adoption in runc 1.3.2 and crun 1.23.
